solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Energetic person keeps a short time for evangelist

indicators.note: one thing that keeps another holds it inside, so the first word wraps round the second

blocks.note: a goer is a lively, energetic person
a spell is a brief period

explanation.surface: A lively preacher fits a quick sermon into a busy schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A gospeller is one who reads or preaches the Gospel, an old term for an evangelist or preacher.

clue.text: No current benefit concerning grandad?

indicators.note: 'no' tells you the letter for the electrical term is to be absent from the word that follows

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
avail means benefit or use, as in 'to no avail'

explanation.surface: Grandad gets no ongoing payout from some scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: AVAIL loses its I to leave AVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Aval is a rare adjective meaning relating to a grandparent, from Latin avus, so the question mark flags an unusual word.

clue.text: Indian army, one cowardly almost in retreat

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the word loses its final letter
an army in retreat goes backwards, so the assembled letters run the other way in this down entry

blocks.note: a means one, as in 'a dozen'
nesh is a dialect word for timid or soft; cut short it loses its H

explanation.surface: An Indian army unit has a coward in its ranks who falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: NESH (northern English dialect for feeble or cowardly) is a Chambers word; A plus NES gives ANES, which reversed is SENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sena is the Hindi word for an army, used in Indian English and in the names of forces and parties.

clue.text: Practice with one flying hawk

indicators.note: flying letters are tossed in the air and land in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Falconry training: practice with one bird in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Accipiter is the genus of short-winged hawks such as the goshawk and sparrowhawk, so it names a kind of hawk.

clue.text: Rather affected French explorer not the first to Canada

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of the name is dropped

blocks.note: Jacques Cartier was the French explorer who claimed Canada for France in the 1530s

explanation.surface: A French explorer, hardly the first European to reach Canada, put on airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Canada' is not wordplay; it simply nods to where Cartier sailed, and the surface asks you to debate who arrived first.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty means pretentiously artistic, so the comparative artier describes something more pretentious or showy.

clue.text: American fellow leaving rough coalfield covered with dust

indicators.note: the two people named are leaving, so their letters go out of the word
rough suggests something knocked about and put together badly, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American worker quits a grim mining area, filthy with coal dust.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and F from COALFIELD, then shuffle the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Colly is an old word for coal soot, and collied means blackened or grimed with it, as Shakespeare used it.

clue.text: Potential energy behind domestic gods

blocks.note: PE is the physics abbreviation for potential energy
nates is the anatomical word for the buttocks

explanation.surface: Physics lesson about stored energy coming after household deities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position word but supplies the buttocks themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The Penates were the Roman household gods who guarded the family store cupboard.

clue.text: Short TV sequence shows missile missing Turkey

indicators.note: a weapon missing something lacks it, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: Trident is the submarine-launched nuclear missile
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: A brief news clip shows a rocket that missed its target in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIDENT minus TR gives IDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ident is the brief station identification clip a broadcaster shows between programmes.

clue.text: One staggering sum shorter after section removed

indicators.note: removed tells you one letter, standing for section, is taken away from the word for shorter

blocks.note: a tot is a sum added up, as in 'tot up'
terser means more brief
S is an abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: An amazing figure gets reduced once part of it is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering sum' reads as a huge amount; really 'staggering' belongs to the definition and 'sum' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily, so a totterer is someone who reels or wobbles about.

clue.text: Fish casserole not completely cooked

indicators.note: not completely means the dish's name is cut short by its final letter
cooked as in falsified, so the letters are doctored into a new order

blocks.note: the word minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A fish stew left undercooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely cooked' reads as one phrase for underdone, but it hides two separate instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: The escolar is an oily, dark-skinned fish of the snake mackerel family found in warm seas.

clue.text: Unconcealed single part of harmonic series

blocks.note: overt means open, not hidden
one means single

explanation.surface: A frank account of one piece of music theory.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is any of the higher partials above the fundamental, which together make up the harmonic series of a note.

clue.text: Smash hit’s number one, complete with soprano upfront

indicators.note: upfront says the letters gathered so far are placed at the beginning, ahead of the remaining piece

blocks.note: to do a job is to complete it
S is the abbreviation for soprano
the first letter of hit

explanation.surface: A chart-topping record whose lead singer is a soprano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash hit' seems a single phrase, but 'Smash' alone is the definition: smash is old slang for loose change.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal slang for money, smash once meaning coins or small change and dosh being cash.

clue.text: Seasonal visitor put nothing over colouring matter

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so these letters are read backwards

blocks.note: Father Christmas visits once a year
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Father Christmas dropped off no presents, just some paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Santalin is the red dye extracted from red sandalwood, a pigment used for staining.

clue.text: Cut two thirds of rough drawing

indicators.note: two thirds of a six-letter word keeps four of its letters, here its closing ones

blocks.note: a sketch is a rough drawing; its final four letters are kept

explanation.surface: An artist reduces a rough sketch by a third.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut lines into a surface such as metal or glass with acid or a tool.

clue.text: Check place to get assistance

blocks.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
aid means help

explanation.surface: Look up where to go for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for a chequered pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is tartan cloth woven in a pattern of crossing stripes, which is a check pattern.

clue.text: Anxiety shown by supporter of Democrat

blocks.note: a fan supports a team or star
of read as to, as in 'the key of the door' meaning the key to it
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A Democrat's backer is visibly nervous before the election.
explanation.definitionFit: The fantods, a word Mark Twain popularised, are a state of nervous fidgets, unease or a fit of the jitters.

clue.text: It gives out when pressed in correctly?

indicators.note: the question mark asks for the words put right, sorted into their correct order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soap pump works only if you push its button properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes a pump that delivers when pushed, so the wordplay doubles as a description of the thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispenser is a device that hands out a measured amount of something, such as soap or cash.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts at soirée not started

indicators.note: not started means the party word loses its opening letter
nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: Fruit and nuts were set out, but the evening party never got going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit and nuts' reads as party snacks; 'nuts' actually belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An etaerio is the botanical term for an aggregate fruit formed from many small fruitlets, as in the raspberry or strawberry.

clue.text: Reluctant trustee initially making one cross

indicators.note: initially says this piece comes at the start, in front of the other word

blocks.note: TR is a dictionary abbreviation for trustee
averse means unwilling

explanation.surface: An unwilling trustee annoys everyone at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like it wants the first letter of trustee, but here it places the whole abbreviation at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse a place is to travel across it, so it is a synonym for crossing.

clue.text: Astronomical work, in essence an old tale of adventure

blocks.note: alma is the Spanish word for soul, a being's essence
a gest or geste is a medieval tale of heroic deeds

explanation.surface: A vast astronomical treatise is basically an old adventure story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Almagest is Ptolemy's second-century treatise on the movements of the stars and planets, the standard astronomy text for centuries.

clue.text: Plodding students struggle endlessly? Hard cheese!

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter of the contest word goes

blocks.note: a sap is a swot, a dull plodding student
an agon is a contest or conflict, from Greek

explanation.surface: Swotting students struggle forever: tough luck!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' is British slang for 'bad luck'; here it is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapsago is a hard green Swiss cheese flavoured with melilot, used grated, so it is literally a hard cheese.

clue.text: Spiders: jumping pair seen leaving back of garden

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, the one kept here
the named letter is leaving, so it goes out of the word
jumping letters leap about and land in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of garden

explanation.surface: Two jumping spiders spotted scuttling off from the end of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' sits next to 'Spiders' as if naming jumping spiders, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Epeira is an old genus name for the common garden orb-weaving spiders, so epeiras are spiders of that kind.

clue.text: Al’s quip being broadcast as satirical stuff?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, like sown seed, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian's wisecrack goes out on air as satire.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasquil, or pasquinade, is a lampoon or satirical squib posted in a public place.

clue.text: Character from Rhodes hosting a dance

indicators.note: a host has a guest inside, so the Greek letter holds the other piece

blocks.note: Rhodes is Greek, and lambda is a Greek letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone from a Greek island throws a dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a person, but in crosswords it often means a letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast, sensual Brazilian couples dance that was a craze around 1990.

clue.text: Man’s on top of a tough youth getting angry

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top of means placed above, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for a man
taken as written
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth with a hard-man image

explanation.surface: A man squares up to a young tough and loses his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Heated describes a person or argument that has become hot-tempered, passionate or furious.

clue.text: Scottish storyteller showing real eccentricity in play

indicators.note: letters in play move about freely, ending up rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
e is the mathematical symbol for the eccentricity of a conic

explanation.surface: A Scottish yarn-spinner shows true oddness on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentricity' looks like an anagram signal but supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leear is a Scots form of liar, and a storyteller is a mild euphemism for someone who tells lies.

clue.text: Accuse falsely, according to some heartlessly

indicators.note: heartlessly means without a heart, so the central letters of the word go

blocks.note: as per means according to
taken as written; its middle two letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Some people cruelly accuse others without grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to cast slurs on someone, attacking their reputation with false charges.

clue.text: Go off defending government’s historic list

indicators.note: a defender surrounds and guards, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: reest is a Scots and dialect verb meaning to go rancid, as bacon does
G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: Leave to protect the government's archive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' suggests leaving, but here it means turning rancid.
explanation.definitionFit: Regest is an archaic word for a register or record, a formal list of entries.

clue.text: Head keeping mum gets stick

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: head and can are both slang for a toilet
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A headteacher who stays silent gets the cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping mum' reads as staying silent; 'mum' is a mother here.
explanation.definitionFit: A caman is the curved stick used in shinty, the Scottish game resembling hockey.

clue.text: Friendly ex-PM accommodating leader of Tories

indicators.note: the leader of a group is at its front, so only the opening letter is wanted
accommodating means giving room to, so one word houses the other

blocks.note: Theresa May was the British prime minister from 2016 to 2019
the first letter of Tories

explanation.surface: A former prime minister gets on well with the party chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Maty is an informal adjective for sociable and pally, behaving like a mate.

clue.text: Sailor, head down rests as before

indicators.note: in a down entry, moving the head down sends the first letter to the bottom

blocks.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor takes a nap with his head lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' marks an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Alt is an obsolete form of halt, a stop or pause, so alts are rests in old usage.

clue.text: Onset of rain stops wet Perth Test

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so the opening letter is taken
something that stops a gap plugs it, so the letter sits inside the word

blocks.note: to pee is to urinate, wet in a crude sense
the first letter of rain

explanation.surface: Rain stops play in a cricket Test match at Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth reads as the Australian Test ground but is the Scottish city, flagging a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pree is a Scots verb meaning to taste or sample, which is to test something.

clue.text: Boundaries hit at last but not one ton

indicators.note: not one says a single letter, for ton, is left out of the group
hit means knocked about, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for ton

explanation.surface: A cricketer finally hits boundaries but doesn't reach a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a hit to the edge for four or six, and a ton is a century of runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuttals are the boundaries where pieces of land meet, the borders of an estate.

clue.text: Israeli intelligence uncovered bones

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters are removed

blocks.note: Mossad is Israel's national intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Israeli spies dig up skeletons.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, the anatomical word for a bone.

clue.text: Network spy leaving tips for young female worker

indicators.note: each word leaves behind its tip, the final letter, before they are joined

blocks.note: a grid is a network of lines
a setter is an old word for a decoy or informer who spies for others

explanation.surface: A spy ring drops off the end of a young woman worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A grisette was a young French working woman, such as a shop girl or seamstress, named after her grey dress.

clue.text: Peter started to get supplied with fuel

blocks.note: Pet is the standard abbreviation for the Epistles of Peter
rolled means got going, as cameras roll

explanation.surface: Peter set off once the tank was filled.
explanation.definitionFit: To petrol a vehicle is to fill its tank with petrol, the British word for gasoline.
